models.inverse_notes: PI=QT*C-FIX given C>0, requiring PI>=0; FIX=QT*C-PI; C=(FIX+PI)/QT given QT>0. Published substitution QT=1400, C=50, FIX=50000 gives PI=20000; forward 1400. At C<=0 no finite required volume exists.
limitations: Demand limits, achievability, cash-flow timing and uncertainty are ignored per the AccountingTools scope: the record answers the volume arithmetic, not whether the volume is attainable.
Loss targets (negative PI), multi-product mix, and post-range parameter drift are out of scope and need their own records.

relationship.original_equation: required unit sales for target profit = (fixed operating cost + target operating profit) / contribution margin per unit
relationship.translation_notes: Direct transcription with symbols FIX (fixed operating cost), PI (target operating profit) and C (contribution margin per unit); the C input triple is byte-identical to the margin record output and the FIX input triple to the cost-adapter output, so both legs bind. sources.evidence: $50,000/month fixed costs with a $50 average unit contribution margin gives a 1,000-unit break-even; adding a $20,000 target profit gives (50,000 + 20,000) / 50 = 1,400 units; adding $10,000 of fixed costs gives (70,000 + 10,000) / 50 = 1,600 units per month.
